definition: Imperious means commanding and domineering; expecting to be obeyed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word imperious. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know imperious should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Grandmother Petra ran Sunday dinner in an imperious style, seating guests with a pointed finger and waving off every offer of help.
A bossy cousin tells everyone where to stand; an imperious one expects the standing to happen unasked — command carried like a birthright.
Tyrannical goes past imperious: the imperious chairman expects obedience, while the tyrannical one has the locks changed on whoever withholds it — manner hardened into rule by force.

Domineering rule bullies its way to control — orders barked, objections flattened, the grip visibly maintained. Imperious rule skips the effort: it assumes control is already its due, and expects obedience before a single order has been spoken.

An overbearing presence presses its weight down on everyone nearby — interrupting, insisting, filling the room. Imperious adds a crown to the weight: not pressure but calm entitlement, the settled certainty that others will comply because compliance is owed.

High-handed describes what power does — deciding without asking, overriding whoever it inconveniences. Imperious describes the manner the power is worn with: command carried like a birthright, so certain of obedience that nothing needs announcing at all.
